source_text: μέρους ἁγίαν καὶ ὑπὸ Θεῷ ζωήν· ἧς ὑποτύπωσις ἀκριβὴς, ἡ σεμίδαλις διὰ δρακὸς ἱερέως ἀναφερομένη σὺν τῷ ἐλαίῳ καὶ τῷ λιβάνῳ. Τὴν γάρ τοι Θεῷ καθιερουμένην ζωὴν, καὶ εἰ γένοιτο τυχὸν ἐκ μέρους, εὐώδη πάντως εἶναι χρὴ, καὶ λιπαρωτάταις ἐλπίσι πιαινομένην. Ἦ οὐκ εὐοσμότατον εἶναι φὴς πᾶν ἔργον ἡμῶν ἀγαθόν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Τί δέ; οὐκ ἐπ' ἀγαθαῖς ἐλπίσι πράττεται πρὸς ἡμῶν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ναί· ἕψεται γὰρ πάντως τὰ παρὰ Θεοῦ. {ΚΥΡ.} Λίβανος δὴ οὖν, καὶ σεμίδαλις ἐλαιόδευτος, τὴν εὐώδη τε καὶ λιπαρωτάτην ἡμῖν ὑπαινίττεται ζωήν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης· ἀλλὰ τίς ἂν γένοιτο πρὸς ἡμῶν ἡ ὡς ἐκ μέρους ἁγία ζωή; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἡ μήτε εἰς λῆξιν πολιτείας ἥκουσα τῆς ἁγιοπρεποῦς, μήτε κατὰ τὴν ἄγαν ἀνῳκισμένην ἰοῦσα τρίβον, ὁποία τις ἦν ἡ Ἰωάννου φωνὴ τυχὸν, ἤγουν τῶν ἁγίων ἀποστόλων· μήτε μὴ ἐκπίπτουσα τοῦ εἶναι σεπτὴ, διά γε τὸ ἡττῆσθαι τυχὸν τῆς ἄγαν ὑποκειμένης που. Ἦ οὐ τῶν ἐν κόσμῳ καὶ παιδοποιῶν ὁ βίος, εἰ διαζῇν ἕλοιντο χρηστῶς, μεμέρισταί πως Θεῷ τε καὶ κόσμῳ, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου φωνήν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Μεμέρισται· πῶς γὰρ οὔ; {ΚΥΡ.} Τύπος οὖν ἄρα ζωῆς τῆς οὐκ εἰσάπαν ἀνακειμένης Θεῷ, μέσης δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ ἐπ' ἄμφω βλεπούσης, ἡ μερικὴ καθιέρωσις τῆς σεμιδάλεως ἦν, τὸ εὐῶδες ἐχούσης καὶ ἱλαρόν· ἣν καὶ εἰς μνημόσυνον ἔσεσθαί φησιν ὁ νόμος, τοῦ δι' ὑπουργίας ἱερατικῆς προσκεκομικότος. Ἀποκερδανοῦμεν δὲ ἀληθῶς τὸ ἐν μνήμῃ κεῖσθαι τῇ παρὰ Θεῷ, δι' ὧν καρποφοροῦντες εὐωδιάζομεν· μεσιτεύοντος τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ Θεῷ προσάγοντος, τὸ[ν] μὲν ὁλοκλήρως ἅγιον, ὡς ἐν τάξει τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων· καὶ μέντοι τὸν μὴ τοιοῦτον εἰσάπαν διὰ τὸ μεμερίσθαι τῷ κόσμῳ, θυσίαν ὥσπερ τινὰ μερικήν. Ἄζυμος δὲ ἡ θυσία. Πρέποι γὰρ ἂν πράττεσθαι καθαρῶς, πᾶν ὅπερ ἂν γένοιτο πρὸς ἡμῶν, εἰς δόξαν Θεοῦ. Καὶ γοῦν ὁ Σωτὴρ, παραιτεῖσθαι προστέταχε, τὸ ἐν μέσαις ἑστῶτα ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ποιεῖσθαι τὰς προσευχὰς, καὶ τὸ ἀμειδὲς ἐν νηστείαις, καὶ τὸ σαλπίζειν ἀκόσμως, κατοικτείροντας ἀδελφούς. Ζύμη γὰρ αὕτη, βεβηλοῦσα τὰ ἱερά. Τὸ δὲ εἰς δόξαν Θεοῦ πραττόμενον, ἐγκλημάτων ἀνθρωπαρεσκείας ἀπηλλάχθαι πρέπει· εἴη γὰρ ἂν οὕτως ἄζυμον ἀληθῶς καὶ ἱερὸν τὸ θύμα. Μερὶς δὲ καὶ βρῶσις τοῖς ἱερεῦσι, τὸ κατάλοιπον τῆς θυσίας. Ἐσθίεται πᾶν ἀρσενικὸν ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ· τοῦ μὲν ἐν ἁγίῳ τόπῳ πρὸς τῶν ἱερέων δαπανᾶσθαι τὰ ἱερὰ, τοῖς μυστικωτέροις ἡμῶν λόγοις τηροῦντος τὸ σέβας· τοῦ δὲ πᾶν ἄρσεν ἐσθίειν, ὑποδηλοῦντος ἀστείως ὡς ἀκαλλές τι χρῆμα καὶ ἀνόσιον ἀληθῶς ὁ μαλακισμὸς τοῖς ἐξειλεγμένοις παρὰ Θεοῦ. Ἀνίερον γὰρ ἀποτελεῖ, καὶ εὐλογίας ἐξίστησι τῆς πνευματικῆς, καὶ ἀμέτοχον ἀποφαίνει τῶν παρὰ Θεοῦ τοῖς ἁγίοις ἐκνενεμη
pass_a_gloss: CYR: [life holy in part and under God,] of which exact under figure (ὑποτύπωσις) the fine flour brought up through handful (δρακός) of priest with the oil and the frankincense. For the life consecrated (καθιερουμένην) to God, even if it happen perhaps in part, must wholly be fragrant (εὐώδη), and fattened (πιαινομένην) with richest (λιπαρωτάταις) hopes. Or do you not say every good work of ours is most fragrant? PALL: very much so. CYR: what then? is it not done by us upon good hopes? PALL: yes; for the things from God will wholly follow (ἕψεται). CYR: frankincense then and fine flour oil moistened (ἐλαιόδευτος) hint at (ὑπαινίττεται) for us the fragrant and richest life. PALL: well you said; but what would be among us the as in part holy life? CYR: the one neither having come into completion/end (λῆξιν) of the saint befitting (ἁγιοπρεποῦς) citizenship (πολιτείας), nor going according to the very high settled (ἀνῳκισμένην) path (τρίβον), of which sort perhaps was the voice of John, or of the holy apostles; nor yet falling away (ἐκπίπτουσα) from being venerable (σεπτή), through being worsted/falling short (ἡττῆσθαι) perhaps of the very [high one] set forth (ὑποκειμένης). Or is not the life of those in the world and child begetting (παιδοποιῶν), if they choose to live through well, divided (μεμέρισται) somehow to God and to world, according to the voice of blessed Paul? PALL: it is divided; how not? CYR: type (τύπος) then of life not entirely devoted (ἀνακειμένης) to God, but middle and as it were looking to both, was the partial (μερική) consecration of the fine flour, having the fragrant and cheerful (ἱλαρόν); which the law says will be for memorial of the one who brought through priestly service. We shall gain (ἀποκερδανοῦμεν) truly the lying in memory (μνήμῃ) that is with God, through things by which bearing fruit (καρποφοροῦντες) we give fragrance; Christ mediating (μεσιτεύοντος) and bringing to God the wholly (ὁλοκλήρως) holy [man] as in rank of whole burnt offerings; and the one not such entirely through being divided to the world, as a kind of partial offering. Unleavened the offering. For it would befit to be done purely everything that may be done by us, unto glory of God. And indeed the Saviour has commanded to refuse (παραιτεῖσθαι) standing in the middle of the marketplaces (ἀγοραῖς) to make prayers, and the unsmiling (ἀμειδές) in fasts, and trumpeting (σαλπίζειν) unbecomingly (ἀκόσμως) when pitying (κατοικτείροντας) brothers. For this [is] leaven (ζύμη), profaning (βεβηλοῦσα) the holy things. What is done unto glory of God must be released from charges of man pleasing (ἀνθρωπαρεσκείας); for thus would be truly unleavened and holy the victim (θύμα). Portion and food for the priests, the remainder of the offering. Every male eats in holy place; the [eating] in holy place by priests of the holy things keeping (τηροῦντος) reverence for our more mystical words; the every male eating, suggesting neatly (ἀστείως) that an ugly (ἀκαλλές) thing and truly unholy (ἀνόσιον) [is] softness (μαλακισμός) for those chosen by God. For it renders [one] unholy (ἀνίερον), removes from spiritual blessing, and shows unsharing (ἀμέτοχον) of the [good things] distributed (ἐκνενεμη-[μένων]) by God to the saints.
pass_b_english: Cyril: An exact figure of this life is the fine flour offered up in the priest’s handful with the oil and the frankincense. For the life consecrated to God, even if perhaps only in part, must surely be fragrant, and enriched with the richest hopes. Or would you not say that every good work of ours is most fragrant?
Cyril: What then? Is it not done by us in good hope?
Palladius: Yes, for what comes from God will surely follow.
Cyril: So the frankincense, and the fine flour moistened with oil, point us to a life that is fragrant and very rich.
Palladius: Well said. But what kind of life among us would be holy in part?

Cyril: One that has not reached the goal of a saintly way of life, and does not walk the path set very high, as perhaps John did, he who was the voice, or the holy apostles; and yet one that does not lose its claim to reverence merely because it perhaps falls short of the lofty path set before us. Or is not the life of those in the world who have children, if they choose to live uprightly, in some way divided between God and the world, in the words of blessed Paul (1 Corinthians 7:33–34)?
Palladius: It is divided; how could it not be?

Cyril: So the partial consecration of the fine flour, which has fragrance and cheerfulness, was a type of the life that is not wholly given over to God, but stands in the middle, as it were, and looks both ways. The law says that this will also be for a memorial (Leviticus 6:15) of the one who brought it through the ministry of the priest. And truly we shall gain this: to be held in God’s remembrance through the things by which we bear fruit and give off fragrance. For Christ acts as mediator and brings to God both the one who is wholly holy, as one ranked among the whole burnt offerings, and the one who is not entirely so, because he is divided and given in part to the world, as a kind of partial offering. The grain offering is unleavened. For it is fitting that whatever we do be done with purity, for the glory of God (1 Corinthians 10:31). Indeed, the Savior commanded us to shun standing in the middle of the marketplaces to make our prayers (Matthew 6:5), a gloomy face when fasting (Matthew 6:16), and sounding a trumpet unbecomingly when we show mercy to our brothers (Matthew 6:2). For this is leaven, which profanes holy things. What is done for the glory of God should be free of any charge of seeking to please men; for in this way the offering would be truly unleavened and holy. The remainder of the grain offering is a portion and food for the priests. Every male eats it in a holy place (Leviticus 6:16–18). That the holy things are consumed by the priests in a holy place preserves the reverence due to our more mystical teachings; that every male eats it aptly suggests that softness is an ugly thing, and truly unholy, in those whom God has chosen. For softness makes a man unholy, cuts him off from spiritual blessing, and leaves him without share in the good things God has allotted to the saints.

choices.why: μαλακισμός rendered ‘softness’ (weakness of will, unmanliness), which Cyril links to Judas in section 24.

PG 68.825. The opening words (‘part holy and under God life’) complete the last sentence of section 22 and are rendered there; this section begins with the relative clause ἧς ὑποτύπωσις, rendered as a fresh sentence. Doubtful reading: ὁποία τις ἦν ἡ Ἰωάννου φωνὴ τυχόν is literally ‘such as perhaps was the voice of John’; taken as John the Baptist, who called himself ‘the voice’ (John 1:23), uncited because the wording is uncertain. Also uncertain: λῆξις (‘end, completion’) rendered ‘completion’; τῆς ἄγαν ὑποκειμένης, set against ἄγαν ἀνῳκισμένην, is taken as ‘the lofty path set before us’; the sense is that a partly holy life does not lose its claim to reverence by falling short of the highest one. ‘Divided between God and the world’ cites 1 Cor 7:33–34 (μεμέρισται). ‘For the glory of God’ echoes 1 Cor 10:31. Matthew 6:5 speaks of synagogues and street corners; Cyril says ‘marketplaces’, a loose allusion. ‘This is leaven’ may echo Luke 12:1 (leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy); left uncited. Grammatically ‘every male is eaten’ (ἐσθίεται πᾶν ἀρσενικόν) plainly means ‘every male eats it’ (Lev 6:16, 18). μαλακισμός rendered ‘softness’ (weakness of will, unmanliness), which Cyril links to Judas in section 24. The first word of col. 828 (ἀγαθῶν, ‘good things’) is rendered at the end of this section to finish the sentence.

changes: ‘brought up by the priest’s handful’ → ‘offered up in the priest’s handful’
‘hint to us at the fragrant and richest life’ calque rewritten
Palladius question reworded to natural order
Genitive absolute μεσιτεύοντος restored as reason (‘For Christ acts as mediator … both … and’); ‘divided and given in part to the world’
Modality: πρέποι ἄν ‘it is fitting’, πρέπει ‘should’ (were ‘ought’/‘must’)
Added Lev 6:16–18 for remainder eaten by every male in a holy place
ἀκαλλές ‘ugly’, ἀστείως ‘aptly’, ἐξίστησι ‘cuts him off’; agency ‘whom God has chosen’ kept
Citations 1 Cor 7:33–34, Lev 6:15, 1 Cor 10:31, Matt 6:5/6:16/6:2 checked
